quotes.text: We know, as has already been noted, AI is so integral to the future, our future success, it cuts across all areas of DOD, but the struggle is, how do we innovate fast enough to keep up with the threat?

Thank you, Mr. Chairman. [...] we now are grappling with this big challenge of how do we take this transformational opportunity that we have that AI is going to present, and what is Congress' role in providing the right guidelines? You know, the guardrails to protect society but also not provide so much, you know, overburdensome regulation that we stifle innovation.

there is a dark side, but there is also a tremendous opportunity. [...] I am interested in how you, as the GAO, are going to be harnessing AI to bring that to bear to assist you. How can we help—how can Congress help you and provide you with the tools and the guidelines you need? Are there any authorities you need?

my understanding is now a lot of these four vendors are leaning on outsourced Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help them assess a veteran's files? Is that accurate, to go through all the documentation there to expedite the process? How is AI being used in this?

Do you have the same level of oversight or eyes on with the technology that they are using as maybe VA claims processors use when they are using AI to help make a claim's determination? [...] what I hear a lot of times from the vendors is, well, it is proprietary. We do not want to share what we are doing. Are you confident that you know what is under the hood in making those decisions?

recent center for Strategic and International Studies report projects that just generative AI alone could require up to 84 gigawatts of additional electricity by 2030, the equivalent of adding another Texas to the grid. So, when you combine that with the growing demand from EVs, semiconductor fabrication plants, data centers, we are headed for a very massive strain on the infrastructure.

I secured $4.5 million dollars in federal funding for the Center for Applied Artificial Intelligence at the University of Florida’s Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences Gulf Coast Research and Education Center.

As an appropriator—also, I'm on the Energy and Water Subcommittee, and we're focused on ensuring Congress is backing the President's AI Action Plan with real resources. [...] Just last week, the House passed the Fiscal Year 2026 Energy and Water Appropriations bill that provided $8.4 billion for the DOE's Office of Science to support high-performance computing, quantum computing, and artificial intelligence research.

Earlier this Congress I led a letter with Congressman McCormick, also on the Science Committee with me, raising concerns about the Biden Administration's proposed AI Diffusion Rule at the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which we believe risk overbroad export controls that could slow U.S. innovation and push some of our allies toward non-U.S. suppliers.
